headline: High-risk shared write-and-network pair: default configs can leak or corrupt work products, while prompt-injection risk is moderate via shared file/STDIN channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files and exchange content through stdin/stdout or shared workspaces, so one agent can feed attacker-controlled text into the other. ms-swift also handles multimodal inputs and configuration files; transformers can run browsers and process documents, increasing the chance it will parse untrusted content as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or pipeline input, THEN prompt-like content in files can influence the other agent.
IF either agent is instructed to treat file contents as trusted instructions, THEN injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate input and output directories per agent.
Strip or label untrusted text before passing between agents.
Disable browser-based ingestion for untrusted documents.
Add a human review step before executing any generated instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches secrets such as hub_token and sdk-token, while transformers has broad network egress and can call the Hugging Face Hub. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive artifacts from agent_a can flow into agent_b and then out over agent_b's network path. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default-style file pipelines, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a writes logs, configs, or checkpoints containing tokens into a shared directory, THEN agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b uploads or transmits those files to a hub or API, THEN leakage occurs.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared workspaces.
Redact tokens from logs and configs before handoff.
Use per-agent directories with restrictive permissions.
Block outbound network access for files that may contain secrets.
Rotate any exposed hub or SDK tokens immediately.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and package installation. That overlap creates a direct race on shared mutable state, and transformers also supports multiple instances, so concurrent writes can corrupt files or dependency state. ms-swift does not state locking or multi-instance support, so the safer reading is high severity.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or virtual environment, THEN concurrent writes can clobber files.
IF either agent installs packages while the other is running, THEN environment drift or corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories and virtual environments.
Serialize package installation steps.
Use file locks around shared mutable resources.
Snapshot or back up the workspace before concurrent runs.
Prefer read-only mounts for inputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can emit model outputs and evaluation artifacts, and transformers is a pipeline framework that can consume those outputs as inputs. If transformers treats ms-swift output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream document processing or serving. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a's generated text or labels without validation, THEN hallucinations or bad metadata propagate.
IF agent_b triggers downstream actions from those outputs, THEN the error becomes operational.
mitigations: Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Add confidence thresholds before downstream use.
Keep a human approval step for high-impact outputs.
Log provenance for each transferred artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. ms-swift handles secrets and broad data classes, while transformers processes documents and multimodal data, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict. Because the rubric requires documented gaps for low severity, this remains low rather than none due to incomplete policy detail.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data under a stricter policy than the other, THEN a compliance mismatch may arise.
IF retention or logging settings differ across the two agents, THEN subject-rights handling can diverge.
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents.
Align logging and retention settings.
Avoid regulated data until residency and certification are confirmed.
Review vendor terms before production use.
